passage:
A farmer used a drone to check crops after a storm. From above, he could see damaged areas that were hard to notice from the ground.
The drone saved time, but the farmer still walked into the field to check soil and plant roots. The aerial view showed where to look. It did not explain everything.
Students visiting the farm learned that new tools can change old work without making old knowledge useless.
The farmer said, "The drone gives me eyes in the sky. My boots still need to touch the ground."
Good decisions often need both wide views and close contact.
